h: Barnstaple before and after the trailers
p: Barnstaple is North Devon's main town, and Boutport Street puts this cinema right on the edge of its historic centre. That means you can stroll in, catch a film and be back among the shops, cafés and pubs within minutes, which makes it a really flexible choice whether you're local or holidaying on the coast.

Rainy days in North Devon tend to send everyone indoors at once, so if the forecast looks grim during the school holidays, book your seats early rather than turning up on the off-chance. The premium seats are worth considering for a long film or a date night, and the bar makes it easy for the grown-ups to turn a family screening into a bit of a treat.
Fill the rest of your day

Just round the corner, the Pannier Market is one of the town's real gems, a long, airy Victorian market hall with stalls that change through the week, and Butchers Row alongside it is a pretty little run of shops with a lot of character. The Queen's Theatre is also on Boutport Street, so you can easily mix a film with a show on another night of your stay.

Down by the river, the historic Long Bridge crosses the Taw, and the Museum of Barnstaple and North Devon sits near the square by the river if you fancy a bit of local history. The Tarka Trail runs right through the town too, a flat, traffic-free route along the old railway line that's perfect for walking or hiring bikes, heading out towards Instow and Bideford with estuary views all the way.

Barnstaple is also a handy base for the big North Devon beaches, with Saunton Sands, Croyde and Woolacombe all within driving distance. A morning of surf, sand and rock pools, followed by an evening film back in town, is a very happy holiday routine. If you're coming by train, the Tarka Line links Barnstaple with Exeter, so a film night doesn't have to mean a car.
Do check the screen number when you book if stairs are an issue, as Screen 1 is the one that's upstairs.
